title: Continuous coalescence parameterizer with shadow-apply and rollback fence
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Build a lightweight continuous parameterizer that converts per-workload telemetry into safe, incremental coalescing (batching + KV cache) configuration proposals, applies them in a shadow/observational mode, and transitions to gradual rollout with automatic rollback fence when regressions are detected. The goal is to reduce per-token cost for hosted and dedicated workloads without increasing tail latency or causing quality regressions. This ticket covers design, implementation of heuristics, telemetry transformations, shadow-apply mechanics, rollout gate logic, and an automated rollback fence integrated with Console alerts and the existing rollout controller.
background: Current batching recommendations are manually triggered or periodic. We lack a closed-loop that (1) profiles evolving workload shapes for sequence length distribution and arrival patterns, (2) generates conservative coalescing parameter deltas, (3) validates them under shadow traffic, and (4) safely flips to staged production with automatic rollbacks on SLO/quality regressions. Customers running bursty interactive workloads show 12-25% token-cost variability that we can address with continuous parameterization. This work ties into the workload profiler and the rollout safety stack.
scope: In scope: telemetry ingestion transforms, heuristic parameter mapper, shadow-apply path, staged rollout integration, rollback fence conditions, Console dashboard panels for proposals and experiments. Out of scope: model architecture changes, new kernel implementations, host-level autoscaler heuristics outside coalescing parameters.
design_overview: 1) Profileer: sample per-route inter-arrival histograms, effective sequence length, KV hit rate, and latency tail percentiles over 5m and 1h windows. 2) Parameterizer: translate profiles into candidate deltas for batch_size_target, max_batch_latency_ms, prefix_cache_ttl_ms, and kv_cache_aggressiveness using heuristics with safety caps. 3) Shadow apply: deploy candidate config into a shadow namespace on a 1% mirror traffic stream and record metrics for 30 minutes. 4) Gate and rollout: compare shadow vs baseline on latency P99, error rate, and evaluation prompt fidelity; if within thresholds, promote to canary with 5-20% traffic over 2 hours and monitor for auto-rollbacks. 5) Rollback fence: automated revert when any safety signal crosses thresholds or when confidence drops based on Bayesian drift detector.
heuristics_summary: Heuristics combine three signals: (A) arrival burstiness (CV and short-window spikes) reduces max_batch_latency_ms and batch_size_target when high; (B) persistent short sequences increase coalescing aggressiveness and reduce prefix_cache_ttl_ms to favor caching small prefixes; (C) high KV hit stability allows more aggressive cache TTL increases. Safety caps: never increase batch_size_target by more than 30% in a single promotion and never change max_batch_latency_ms by more than ±20% without multi-window confirmation.
metrics_and_thresholds: Primary metrics: per-route P50/P95/P99 latency, token-per-request cost, request error rate, prompt-eval similarity (for quality checks), KV hit ratio. Thresholds (initial): P99 latency delta <= +10ms absolute and <= +7% relative; error rate delta <= +0.05% absolute; token-cost reduction >= 3% for promotion; prompt-eval similarity drop <= 0.7% absolute. Bayesian drift detector alpha=0.01 used to flag anomalous divergence.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: unit tests and integration test harness (local synthetic traces). Phase 1: internal canary on non-customer workloads (shadow only). Phase 2: opt-in customers + gradual canary 5% -> 20% -> 50%. Phase 3: default-on for eligible routes with cooling period. Each promotion has automated health checks and a safety window of 2 hours; failing a check triggers immediate rollback and an incident record.
observability: Add Console panels: 'Parameterizer proposals' list, per-proposal shadow vs baseline comparison, per-route TTL and batch_size heatmap, and an experiment timeline. Emit proposal telemetry events: proposal.id, route, creator=parameterizer, candidate_config, baseline_snapshot, shadow_result_summary, decision. Link shadow tests to existing tracing and traces should include config tag. Dashboards: cost impact (tokens/$) and quality regression rollups.
testing: Automated unit tests for heuristics with synthetic workload specs, integration tests against the shadow path simulator, end-to-end test that runs a short shadow experiment and asserts rollback on injected regression, and a load test suite on preprod with replayed customer traces. We'll add property-based tests that assert safety caps hold for random workload inputs.
acceptance_criteria: Parameterizer service converts 1h/5m telemetry into candidate coalescing configs with safety caps
Shadow-apply flow runs for a candidate on mirrored 1% traffic and produces summary metrics within 30 minutes
Console shows proposal and shadow comparison with links to traces and the proposal ID
Automated gate promotes a candidate to staged canary only if thresholds are met and rolls back automatically when thresholds are violated
Integration tests simulate a quality regression and confirm rollback fence triggers within the safety window
implementation_steps: Define telemetry transform proto (fields: route, window_start, arrival_histogram_buckets, seq_len_histogram, kv_hit_rate, p50/p95/p99) and wire to metrics pipeline
Implement heuristic mapper in a new lightweight parameterizer service with pluggable rules and safety caps
Add shadow apply support to rollout controller and a small mirror hook that tags shadow traffic
Emit proposal events to Console backend and add a new proposals table in the Console UI
Implement gate comparator and Bayesian drift detector library integration
Write e2e and load tests; run internal canary and collect results; iterate on heuristics
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive changes increase tail latency. Mitigation: conservative default caps and shadow validation on mirrored traffic.
Risk: Quality regressions undetected by simple metrics. Mitigation: integrate prompt-eval similarity checks and sample human review for early customers.
Risk: Telemetry sparsity on low-traffic routes. Mitigation: require minimum traffic thresholds and fall back to cohort-level recommendations.
Risk: Increased resource usage for shadow runs. Mitigation: cap shadow traffic to 1% and reuse existing idle capacity windows for experiments.
open_questions: What is the minimum traffic threshold to generate reliable proposals per route? Proposed default: 1000 requests/hour.
Should we allow customers to opt-out of automated promotions via API or Console toggle? (product decision)
How long should cooling and observation windows be for routes identified as high-variance? Proposed: 24 hours cooling after a promotion
